6E64B240DFE70131B13C68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

6E643D90DFE70131B13B68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

6E629290DFE70131B13768A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

6AF06046C909451AB911021C9EFC1002.description: Organize and develop artistic ideas and works.

comments: See standard 1.OA.6 for a list of mental strategies.

6D1A3830DFE70131AF8268A86D17958E.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

6D19D500DFE70131AF8168A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

6D194170DFE70131AF7F68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

6D18F440DFE70131AF7E68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

6D1780C0DFE70131AF7A68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.
6D16E640DFE70131AF7868A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

707B4990DFE70131B56A68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (e.g., toss, throw, hurl) and closely related adjectives (e.g., thin, slender, skinny, scrawny).

707AF030DFE70131B56968A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe foods that are spicy or juicy).

707A90A0DFE70131B56868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

707A4110DFE70131B56768A86D17958E.description: Use glossaries and beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases.

7079EAD0DFE70131B56668A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of the meaning of individual words to predict the meaning of compound words (e.g., birdhouse, lighthouse, housefly; bookshelf, notebook, bookmark).

70799D00DFE70131B56568A86D17958E.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., addition, additional).

707950C0DFE70131B56468A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known word (e.g., happy/unhappy, tell/retell).

7078EB00DFE70131B56368A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

7078A2C0DFE70131B56268A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 2 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

70781320DFE70131B56068A86D17958E.description: Compare formal and informal uses of English.

7077C840DFE70131B55F68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

70772130DFE70131B55D68A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

7076D6B0DFE70131B55C68A86D17958E.description: Generalize learned spelling patterns when writing words (e.g., cage → badge; boy → boil).

70767BC0DFE70131B55B68A86D17958E.description: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.

70762340DFE70131B55A68A86D17958E.description: Use commas in greetings and closings of letters.

7075BF80DFE70131B55968A86D17958E.description: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names.

70756720DFE70131B55868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

70751BB0DFE70131B55768A86D17958E.description: Produce, expand, and rearrange complete simple and compound sentences (e.g., The boy watched the movie; The little boy watched the movie; The action movie was watched by the little boy).

7074CC10DFE70131B55668A86D17958E.description: Use adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

70746920DFE70131B55568A86D17958E.description: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs (e.g., sat, hid, told).

7073B090DFE70131B55368A86D17958E.description: Form and use frequently occurring irregular plural nouns (e.g., feet, children, teeth, mice, fish).

70731A50DFE70131B55168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

70722A50DFE70131B54E68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

7071D450DFE70131B54D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

70718130DFE70131B54C68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

7070CFC0DFE70131B54A68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

70702070DFE70131B54868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

706FD7D0DFE70131B54768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

706F4380DFE70131B54568A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

706EEE00DFE70131B54468A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

706E7F00DFE70131B54368A86D17958E.description: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or recounts of experiences when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

706E1F50DFE70131B54268A86D17958E.description: Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences.

706D8F60DFE70131B54068A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.

706D4460DFE70131B53F68A86D17958E.description: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

706CF6C0DFE70131B53E68A86D17958E.description: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.

706CAAA0DFE70131B53D68A86D17958E.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.

706C5370DFE70131B53C68A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

706C06B0DFE70131B53B68A86D17958E.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 2 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

706B23C0DFE70131B53868A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

706AD2D0DFE70131B53768A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

706A7A70DFE70131B53668A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7069E0C0DFE70131B53468A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

70698A50DFE70131B53368A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

70693170DFE70131B53268A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

706219A0DFE70131B53068A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

7060C600DFE70131B52C68A86D17958E.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

70607D30DFE70131B52B68A86D17958E.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., read a number of books on a single topic to produce a report; record science observations).

706032B0DFE70131B52A68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

705FE220DFE70131B52968A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

705F9040DFE70131B52868A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed by revising and editing.

705EB2D0DFE70131B52568A86D17958E.description: Write narratives in which they recount a well-elaborated event or short sequence of events, include details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide a sense of closure.

705E65A0DFE70131B52468A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement or section.

705E12C0DFE70131B52368A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply reasons that support the opinion, use linking words (e.g., because, and, also) to connect opinion and reasons, and provide a concluding statement or section.

705D2810DFE70131B52068A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

705C7A80DFE70131B51E68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

705C0810DFE70131B51D68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

705BB180DFE70131B51C68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

705B6800DFE70131B51B68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

705B1E50DFE70131B51A68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

705ACE10DFE70131B51968A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

705A7690DFE70131B51868A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7059E5E0DFE70131B51668A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

70599E80DFE70131B51568A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

70595440DFE70131B51468A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

7058B880DFE70131B51268A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

70586FB0DFE70131B51168A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

705823C0DFE70131B51068A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

7057C540DFE70131B50F68A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

70576CC0DFE70131B50E68A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

7056BD00DFE70131B50C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.

70566AA0DFE70131B50B68A86D17958E.description: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.

7055FBB0DFE70131B50A68A86D17958E.description: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.

705597E0DFE70131B50968A86D17958E.description: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.

70553FF0DFE70131B50868A86D17958E.description: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.

7054F5A0DFE70131B50768A86D17958E.description: Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words.

7054AC70DFE70131B50668A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

7053C390DFE70131B50368A86D17958E.description: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 2—3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

70536A40DFE70131B50268A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

705320A0DFE70131B50168A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.

7052C460DFE70131B50068A86D17958E.description: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.

705264A0DFE70131B4FF68A86D17958E.description: Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.

7051A110DFE70131B4FD68A86D17958E.description: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.

70515770DFE70131B4FC68A86D17958E.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.

70510CB0DFE70131B4FB68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.

705054C0DFE70131B4F968A86D17958E.description: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.

704FE0B0DFE70131B4F868A86D17958E.description: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.

704F9500DFE70131B4F768A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

704EAE90DFE70131B4F468A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories and poetry, in the grades 2—3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

704E5780DFE70131B4F368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

704DB170DFE70131B4F168A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story (e.g., Cinderella stories) by different authors or from different cultures.

704D5890DFE70131B4F068A86D17958E.description: Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot.

704CA100DFE70131B4EE68A86D17958E.description: Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including by speaking in a different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud.

704C4E10DFE70131B4ED68A86D17958E.description: Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action.

704C02C0DFE70131B4EC68A86D17958E.description: Describe how words and phrases (e.g., regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.

704B6BA0DFE70131B4EA68A86D17958E.description: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges.

704B1E50DFE70131B4E968A86D17958E.description: Recount stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.

704AC230DFE70131B4E868A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

7049A660DFE70131B4E568A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

70495A30DFE70131B4E468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

70491020DFE70131B4E368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

7048BE60DFE70131B4E268A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

70486780DFE70131B4E168A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

7047D3A0DFE70131B4DF68A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

704789A0DFE70131B4DE68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

70473C70DFE70131B4DD68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

70468D80DFE70131B4DB68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

70464380DFE70131B4DA68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

7045E670DFE70131B4D968A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

70452E00DFE70131B4D768A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

4DA82E1AF2F34F3687B712A76E50A65B.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, intended audience, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.

071EACEAF2C34F27B01CEF091FB800DD.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) in order to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source and noting any discrepancies among the data.

10E753280164414B9EFB327B9CF00558.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; synthesize comments, claims, and evidence made on all sides of an issue; resolve contradictions when possible; and determine what additional information or research is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.

29748D80915944CCB51990C2B273A938.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that probe reasoning and evidence; ensure a hearing for a full range of positions on a topic or issue; clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions; and promote divergent and creative perspectives.

C6568F90DEB84BF9948221BE850621A6.description: Collaborate with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making, set clear goals and deadlines, and establish individual roles as needed.

2D849C25FF4A40C6BEB9B586FFC1A9CE.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

35A8C7CA20AC4C6084583E8F9CC14E67.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range variety of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) on grades 11–12 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

9C7F133996914C5696A42C1CAB1D5C14.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

1C6CD665440148D8BD97EF5A2027A2CE.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

B19C55D140DD4EB390B05DE7EF05C4D9.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

F9F112207F294E93A6506E69C8847CFF.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

0DA9E7DDC61443E8BC7B6C91E057D309.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

BE87603E23C043DFB9B233BEB8F26978.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

72C280CB92DD4B12895E14D110329B60.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences; independently select writing topics and formats for personal enjoyment, interest, and academic tasks.

BAFB9FE9901F4A059F7C33C6A524128F.description: Apply grades 11–12 Reading standards for literary nonfiction to writing.

0560764D883841D2AB418193E23F0794.description: Apply grades 11–12 Reading standards for literature to writing.

49680C88E83747359CF50E45735769B4.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and overreliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation.

D14278DD2167456B8A9DEE51141D60A0.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

6AB91035B0474C00A43AB1028E2CCB7F.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

6A61DEECD568467BB4E925118263854E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products in response to ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

B8E97C24095248B396C7C8F76F87A156.description: Use a writing process to develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of Language standards 1–3 up to and including grades 11–12.)

C7C367A933EB464EA6D4B57BDBDB593E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, style and tone are appropriate to grade-specific task, purpose, and audience.

044DE4E25BAD474FA85750C6F95FCD2C.description: Provide a conclusion (when appropriate to the genre) that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative or creative text.

4875525275854386842489ED357E751A.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, figurative and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

DB49CA5BD99243538E2758FFA5FF314E.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution).

DF4C1F492CDB4A79983CA49A164B6E49.description: Use literary or narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

A1E760841FD04F89AA5648C95D093736.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

87CDF5F57E1F40AFA59CCA12739D7043.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

92CB6CAB6CE64B6B88FBFEBF82698CCF.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

4A5058FBFC7C483C9B874F9F70267305.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

012E8C410B6548888A874B1BCFB409D2.description: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

4ECB0188F09E4E5998F6C03CEF1D0D92.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

6458DAD36D8B4CD1B8695ADEEA746829.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

96DC68F9F74F449D852CF319F3EE9838.description: Use transitional words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

25D505A87E004C23BFC4C761D2FE81E3.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

BB429ADBD24940738FDD208B6D84A6A0.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

71C7D94D4BAF4CC8A190476F17FE75D2.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

041B8EAB195D4BA7B307D070C2797FEA.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

DE3B58791F304C99A708A076365A5D0A.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

2A3CE81E8F2B45F5A7276C0EB65CE604.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

2E17EAA922B84670BC9B225F38642770.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

0E23868A6A4E4AB9AE2CFE7D237FC12F.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

EDD5C245F4BD4F54AC8D98CDF502B66B.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

86F48897E7114FB9BC1A4D6979EB967E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, propose, and audience.

BCE70D5944934532B0FF98DB0EEF47A8.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, ad well-structured event sequences.

2E0C61C2DF8E4E349CBAF6D3661C4B32.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

F964704A62EF41A189A5763841FC45A3.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

56A206DD45494BE1906B77C32A614807.description: Read and comprehend grade level texts for academic tasks.

18BEFC3DE32040E9B1545140C630A440.description: By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literary nonfiction and informational texts in the grades 11-CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range. A5FCF5101E97447CA66E18AAE006322F.description: Delineate (break down) and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. and global texts, including the application of founding principles and use of legal reasoning and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy.

7246899D74774E81A7360DDB1EB76BEF.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, verbally, quantitatively) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

AA351DE813E84D84A3A0F8DDE53FF3CE.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to its overall rhetorical effectiveness.

D2F51B1699704E84B98CAFAB7040CA0D.description: Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

5A00DFA4D418432CA25D1FF40E378E22.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text.

44FB76ED742C4C01AA4ADA82952D518C.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the text.

370B7283F0FA46AAA4EC10F1759C47CC.description: Determine two or more central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; provide an objective summary of the text to support analysis.

0F945F58B5FB4C33B4C753C990FBF038.description: Analyze how point of view and/or author purpose requires distinguishing what is directly stated in text and what is implied.

4ADFFA6073264A50A2E0F922A4FD7C49.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

BD7857A7688E45259DB6E5CDACB5B66E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language.

F75F119C1A1E445D921FE8CB2EF1A930.description: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, how the characters are introduced and developed).

3C00E62A03AC42D9812180D7F0766562.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the text to support thematic analysis.

5B27B664A0D24B178C80B058FCBE6314.description: Accurately cite strong, relevant, and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferentially, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

947D797FA51A4201954D44A4DE41EED0.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

953C44A187B043EBA73A03EE15132F73.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

A6A4BF9E8520422B9F6C4DE80F4BA405.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

107814848B2A4FE6B35D2D64EBF2C373.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

E5EC0B130AE842929CCA58763773B683.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

7E44D9578D63479285BAF6C4DBFF4E1A.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

C0DB2AE765674ECDB45A3E9CD74D892A.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

8FD9B354DF564E4893679E4BB9BD01FC.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

E121ABC46F1B482AA088AB98E0F0D70B.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

F114B1802D7B4CFFB4CAF18A37414248.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

7B75A8E0AEDC476198D82CD54D7E9EE4.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

EBF58207BB7642C0ABCC40FED382A876.description:
Prepare and interpret formal end-of-fiscal period financial statements.
 Prepare a balance sheet
 Prepare an income statement and calculate component percentages
 Prepare an owners' equity statement
 Journalize and post adjusting and closing entries
 Prepare a post-closing trial balance.

3C65AAF819EF4056913DF9D3608EE8B8.description:
Complete and analyze an accounting worksheet.
 Prepare a trial balance from the general ledger
 Analyze and calculate adjusting entries on the worksheet
 Extend and complete the worksheet to assess a net gain or net loss

447B489B0B334A498F43464BF5C83A35.description:
Analyze and complete payroll using appropriate accounting practices.

 Calculate gross earnings using regular and overtime hours
 Analyze and compute payroll deductions
 Determine net pay and prepare payroll checks

Post information from journals into general and subsidiary ledgers.

general or subsidiary ledger.
 Post column totals from a journal to the general ledger.

Assess the accounting equation as a guide to journalize transactions.

 Specify various journals such as general, multi-column, and special
 Apply the double-entry system of accounting to record business
transactions
 Total, prove, and rule journals
 Computer software may be utilized to complete transactions.

17E70006E3504CF6B91889B1D5429A79.description:
Examine, analyze, and categorize financial transactions.

 Analyze usage of T accounts
 Analyze transactions into debit and credit parts
 Create and maintain proper file maintenance for all accounts

FA87CCA2E2384481838CA8F654421544.description: Demonstrate the basic principles and procedures of the accounting cycle.

Comprehend proper cash management techniques and prepare
necessary documents and transactions.

reconciliation

 Discuss ethical issues concerning business cash management

12BC6CB826A348308DC082BD6BAC80C3.description:
Compare and contrast various types of business ownership and
accounting principles that apply.
 Classify business ownership as sole proprietorship, partnership, or
corporation

Identify career opportunities in the accounting profession.

within the accounting profession
 Discuss ethical implications pertaining to the accounting profession

17A2BB275BC34B509D14A3F35BADFB05.description: Examine the role of accounting in business.

489E899BA8984BD09220D1FA5674F2E0.description: Given a number(s) from 1–20, count out that many objects.

F9320B78032944B8869FD6573985B53A.description: When counting, answer questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or and as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration.

170C95382C8549F4B9B49AC96486C2FA.description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

A6B80D18165D499797A998FA6694F7D0.description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. (cardinality) The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.

51ECE8BEAD99433DBE132383A3EC578C.description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object. (one-to-one correspondence)

3C5316DBD2A44DBCA7B58502424F0818.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

DF30EDBC2E814F97A57F79D801F2098D.description: Count to tell the number of objects.

EFFB8FD0643A47BAA14AA725CDBC6739.description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

CB6446075148462DBCBC25FFCF5E7C82.description: Count forward beginning from any given number within 100 (instead of having to begin at 1). Count backwards beginning from any given number within 20.

26E8770BCB1446979E2C72E6CB503025.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

F231BC422A4C4D27ADA2371ACE706B44.description: Know number names and the count sequence.

2DAE01C42F634B5087AEB753F38F2F10.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

BA1B9DCF05904615954B51E134F3F009.description: Look for and make use of structure.

41B9AAC833C64A8CAF26446761D66AE4.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

582CF9AD14324979A0AF442E24E70B7A.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: South Dakota State Standards for Mathematics

225C850F7B894B759A51B74029B1E143.description: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

B401AD6181DA4A0D90B0025EA05E3591.description: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.

B13AB27F67A84AAEABC3185F26788855.description: Understand that in adding two-digit numbers (sums within 100) add tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.

4129002DA0A446719781003CAA422822.description: Add within 100, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

0870599F39EE47E395D7D4634060D8CE.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operation to add and subtract

96148DE5B76143E8988C960758A4B997.description: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols <, =, and >.

2A8687BD452741F390B04221EA5F451E.description: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).

27E52E7D9D3A4BB1A8034E89E123888B.description: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

AE17A11806774F318CAB4426553DAF32.description: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones — called a "ten."

980508A67DE5453085B3ECC8906AB442.description: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:

BF51515DBCE0443D89B967FFD81903ED.description: Represent a number of objects with a written numeral.

6EFDC4C1A48C48628D28A56B6B75D8F7.description: Count on from any given number.

C21FDEC6CD714D2BB1F952FFBF591B6E.description: Number and Operation in Base Ten

C1204E3EA3E94D0BB9B5C3D2E28E5AF8.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

AD35ADE42D484F26AB7276E4EF445620.description: Compose and Identify regular and irregular two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) and compose three-dimensional shapes (cubes, spheres, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape. (Students do not need to master formal names such as "right rectangular prism.")

55D918CA92A0465A8F64F0BD18D0A719.description: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.

F1214B33CC2F49EEA1BB71158E00822F.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

7DC18796D8F640ACACAEE9E7C2D63716.description: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.

51DA58941BDD422486C752EDF0D82CF0.description: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps.

1A953B53EA5F4333BFBAED51EDB4E05B.description: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.

1242F72FB828416BB9B99ED7392EE6A8.description: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.

673D2EE0E4894B9E8407AA955033FA62.description: Identify nickels and understand that five pennies can be thought of as a nickel. Identify dimes and understand ten pennies can be thought of as a dime. Count the value of a set of coins comprised of pennies, nickels, and dimes.

46A24BBE5E234E9AAB9B4B62A13D7E96.description: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.

1CB36E78A9574BCCBC1295ACB0842B80.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating to three whole numbers. For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 +? = 11, 5 = ? – 3, 6 + 6 = ? .

30DF163134934969A606D22FFB11D6ED.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false. For example, which of the following equations are true and which are false? 6 = 6, 7 = 8 – 1, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2.

68CC5F2DDD7A4027AFFD4860C68D63CA.description: Work with addition and subtraction equations.

1DD26AD86F7040E89D90D0D739FA0FE0.description: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 – 4 = 13 – 3 – 1 = 10 – 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 – 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

38297D037360410898ACC5234F6B3399.description: Understand counting on as addition and counting back as subtraction e.g. 5, (6,7,8) means 5 + 3 and 5, (4,3,2) means 5-3.

85C522976EE649CA97A7AD30369CD5E1.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem. For example, subtract 10 – 8 by finding the number that makes 10 when added to 8.

366D3DF94FD3475CBBB510FBD07597C5.description: Apply commutative, associative, and additive identity properties of operations as strategies to add. (Students need not use formal terms for these properties.) Examples: If 8 + 3 = 11 is known, then 3 + 8 = 11 is also known. (Commutative property of addition.) To add 2 + 6 + 4, the second two numbers can be added to make a ten, so 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12. (Associative property of addition.) 8 + 0 = 8 (Additive Identity property)

E2C4845E400A4F609FC8C00363443F92.description: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between additions and subtraction.

E15EBA881EF54D38B9B4324F70146493.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

DAC4C4C420FA4292B5305C2873AF6800.description: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

01CEFDFEBC6D4EC0BCCC6DD32AE7C92E.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

1B128AFA272D4C4D8C4A63D66F2D8B84.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

BD50F9A3E0164882AE1C9D6EB912AAE4.description: Look for and make use of structure.

558AC6A9E4D74281B77737EA316AC075.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

4CC6451F8D4B4681BC19AD0AF1A1CB44.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: South Dakota State Standards for Mathematics

A87970BA7A6647AB9680F64E4BD6448F.description: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations. (Explanations may be supported by words, drawings or objects.)

A86B32E45D024F09A124B2C442CEFFE7.description: Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100–900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100–900.

7AE7898296824B8890A7E7107683F15C.description: Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.

7BC6B4EBE7714BE39F1E64831E2C6AF7.description: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

40ECD230A4FF43EDB019387BCD9F4D79.description: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

30688D6327FE4D7AA47F47F7B744DFA7.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operation to add and subtract.

347C82B5CA8F4688992F268A88F7D252.description: Compare, two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

D85E83B9A942425AB14708208A75F60C.description: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals (standard form), number names (word form), and expanded form.

F2826917DC674632BDDF5229C301D82B.description: Count within 1000; skip-count by 5s, 10s, and 100s, starting from any number in its skip counting sequence.

1D34758E4181449BBE5F46CDAF9DE7C7.description: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

ABEB39F22CB04D3F8EA32C98EC864AC5.description: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a "hundred."

E367DA9079CC460784A6FC88F5B138A3.description: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases:

99BDBF7C1ECF4E6196CECACD812745D5.description: Number and Operation in Base Ten

CF3CEEEEFFCE4679A22380492DC3F42B.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

970AF110C3C3457FB7B3215F5027568F.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.

26F6043A37144A1A899E5672D35AF7CE.description: Recognize, identify, and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces; to include triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes. (Sizes are compared directly or visually, not compared by measuring.)

2AB2D8938777424C908521E66CFCE118.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

8FC0DF314F1B4C6581EC571D5C59AAE0.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, …, and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

D4469702343F4EB2A8B8EAD1F7584378.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

6A216B64C2E74C42BF466771BAB7ADBF.description: Relate addition and subtraction to length.

50FB8B3D2CC14E0EB44511F2A6AE8FA0.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.

9A91C3A32A9D4E80900441652A1BE6FF.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

C4C857C8131D4247A0439B6FF23C4B43.description: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.

BD2F480A04EA4D938D8E879A760C479D.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.

D66D141EF20C4C4A9E226503BBD2AFEB.description: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.

EB13D3751C654C1BABA0099452731ED2.description: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.

E00903E21EE846CDB50FA5C27B37BCE4.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units.

79D69D9C62694E5CBCF0EA17B88B0A72.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.

1E5083DF66D44F29A030EE722AC2AC34.description: Recognize and know the value of coins up to one dollar.

347977BC0E0E439FACE44FF7355B6DF0.description: Identify and count coins and bills and apply that understanding to solve word problems.

626B682221B64C06B06074AAEAE06387.description: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

7623D386F1AA40668DE33B59FBEAB594.description: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.

17BC7B9D12B148DC8E7511820D08FA2B.description: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by 2s; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.

F58A9B19C89546E7BD7CE73271F23C34.description: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.

0253C674B7874BC5A1C938D0ABD1E7A4.description: By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.

20BCB855232A487987AE293BD249FFFF.description: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. (See standard 1.OA.6 for a list of mental strategies.)

CC3317E763FA4C07960653A36E7E872F.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

C347BA2CD7C346C0BD0D49BCB2566736.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

1104E3A72CC541A9B63ED177D9010BF7.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

8B0A9BFACDF9476D8E3A13110E0B3E88.description: Look for and make use of structure.

D96E27DF799C40CA9B0EE4FD5619782C.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

63EC45CB693D4386A9839A8B5208C5E2.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: South Dakota State Standards for Mathematics

0598F71F30A44C3E8BAB72AF731851ED.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols < , =, or >.

1ABF36A99B0145B8A6436097D0AF69B4.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.

EF64428F378E4E6CA5EA63D7A9532DB8.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., ½ = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3. Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

ED2EB301C67E43E4B7852523DA74DE23.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.

6C9AF64229C54786989F233B900FC080.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size. Note - Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.

B90009166CC34303B916145E4824C217.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

A3B028ED9157482FB2889EFB4FA66E0A.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

46CBCC27D2F34C9C95F09F669C5266E6.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

2AB279A37EAE4EC5B118C8CC15964111.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts (example: 1 part out of 4 equal parts is the same as ¼); understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b. (example: ¾ is the same as 3 one-fourths (¼, ¼, ¼)

C99C78E434F040E89C270E41F4D4DE69.description: Develop understanding of Fractions as numbers.

EB72A6F4883E4B139F5D6EAAA1ED8E26.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10–90 (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

E46EABA490B74931978BA72E8D2ACFCB.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

A72EF4FE4DF04A098EF3108989B62A63.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

1084A8AB4D9641A58A7CEA48FA037D17.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operation to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

83902A7038744CD786DB51E29F3823BB.description: Number and Operation in Base Ten

23DB57B16C8F44A5B479F74F7142D94D.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole. For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as ¼ of the area of a shape.

BE8E63768954435EB1E120AA9848D89F.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

C003C27D4BA1450782A3A2C5DBC63726.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

43DE8B9D6550424B8E516AE04CBE4A52.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units— whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

8AFAB83608AA40D093F79C57DE593F07.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

41D7C411F76745B7A5FE93F2B920DDA6.description: Determine the value of a collection of money using dollar sign and decimal point appropriately. Understand that the digits to the right of the decimal represent parts of a whole dollar.

DC2DBF90478F41FF823DDEE2A317B4A6.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

FFD28E8ADFD340ECBFDA13526D56FDE3.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.
