The student tells of the Norman Conquest, the rule of King John of England, the signing of the
Magna Carta, and the emergence of parliament. H

9B3FE23EE0CB4012B26B1821E7108101.description:
The student explains the origin of the Great Schism of 1054, the Investiture Controversy, and
the Concordat of Worms. H

73036982EB114264BF0278530DA6D280.description:
The student describes and explains Christian and Muslim art and architecture in the Middle
Ages. H

9C5E36CE784D45729762D7AD18604398.description:
The student explains the development and practice of feudalism in European societies,
including the expectations of each class, and of slavery in the Middle East, Africa, and Asia. H

FA578374417048489F41C200A56C8F37.description:
The student explains the historical events and effects of the Carolingian dynasty, the
establishment of the Holy Roman Empire, the Viking invasions, and the rule of Vladimir of
Kiev. H

984F2C0F3A4A421194EA869EE22ADC3F.description:
The student explains the major historical events, cultural features, stories, and religious
contributions of early Muslims, including the origins and role of the Qur’an, the preservation
of Greek thought, and expansions in science, philosophy, and mathematics. H

DB5F533FB6D14CB29BE0CAFEFE8507E8.description:
The student explains the major ideas and events surrounding the life of Mohammed and their
historical effects, including the founding and spread of Islam and divisions between Sunnis and
Shi’ites. H

4A1245983173431FB4552C6F07930ECE.description:
The student explains the establishment of monasteries, the practices of monasticism, the
preservation of ancient thought, and their role in the Middle Ages. H

C63AF22BE56C44FEB2DF8F43C0269179.description:
The student explains the ways in which society changed with the fall of the Roman Empire and
the perpetuation of the Eastern Roman Empire in Constantinople, including the role of
Christianity. H

3657EBA4B8B54B3B90DEB3B1BDACB989.description:
The student explains the origins and cultures of the major indigenous tribes of Europe around
500, including the Ostrogoths, Burgundians, Franks, Visigoths, Lombards, Saxons, Angles,
Britons, Celts, Slavs, and Norse. H

4282247A85F24723A91AD24F859EA012.description: The student demonstrates knowledge and understanding of the Middle Ages.

484BAF48248E4A14BC37F165F0A2FA13.description:
The student explains the role of the papacy and historical figures in establishing Christianity
and Roman law in Europe and the near east, including the Christian church fathers, Augustine
of Hippo, Leo I, and Justinian. H

EA8D17FDDD554D5FBA2FFF0E7DCD715A.description:
The student explains the origins of the barbarian invasions and the other factors that led to
the fall of the Roman Empire, including the power of the military establishment, political
corruption, and economic instability arising from opulence. H

89B99BD3BA78436CB9E4B12284650694.description:
The student compares the religion of the Christians to that of the Hebrews and of polytheist
religions, including monotheism, the Trinity, the belief in Jesus of Nazareth as divine, the
redeeming of a person’s sins, the individual worth of each person, and equal moral obligations
of each person regardless of class or authority. H

AEDD5DEFD8994E4988A2D3E9B157DB25.description:
The student explains the major historical events, cultural features, stories, and religious
contributions of the early Christians, including the origins and role of the Bible. H

19946BE40F544ED5AE8C40EC8DFFD5C3.description:
The student explains the major events during the rule of Constantine, including the
legalization of Christianity and the moving of the Roman capital to Constantinople. H

E7709ADB21DE4F2D84EB402C9ED3EEC4.description:
The student explains the major historical events and cultural features of the Roman Empire,
including under the rule of Octavian Caesar, the Julio-Claudian dynasty, Trajan, Hadrian,
Marcus Aurelius, and Diocletian. H

9BAE5E51EA71459982121269C618B7D1.description:
The student explains the factors that accounted for the Roman Empire’s relative stability and
longevity, including its military organization and tactics, the Pax Romana, decentralized
administration, the taxation system, a standard currency, and the road system. H

23B8D18CB6D14795ACFA9D2FDF9760F8.description:
The student explains the major ideas and events surrounding the life of Jesus of Nazareth and
their historical effects, including the establishment of early Christian churches, the spread of
Christianity, and persecutions of Christians. H

61233447E0FC4E729B256A8CB9A41601.description:
The student explains the origins and major events of the Roman civil wars and the
triumvirates, including the ideas and actions of Cato the Elder, Cicero, Julius Caesar, and
Octavian Caesar. H

4E3ADC91E7DB45B7BC786717A659A479.description:
The student explains the causes, warfare, strategy, outcomes, and effects of the Punic Wars,
including the battles of Cannae and Zama and the roles of Hamilcar Barca, Hannibal, and
Scipio Africanus. H

261FE373257D4100B5D06A79474EB60E.description:
The student explains the major cultural features and contributions of Rome, including in
architecture, engineering, sculpture, poetry, slavery, the Latin language, and the histories of
Livy, Tacitus, and Polybius. H

320F78532C8F4C01AA72F4FCDB62E461.description:
The student explains the social and political organization of the Roman Republic and the
influence of its governing principles and institutions, including the rule of law, the separation
of powers, ideas of civic duty, and representative government. HC

32EBCB4442DA44B39EEFCC052E9B2C28.description:
The student explains the stories and events surrounding the founding of Rome and the Roman
Republic. H

5DF4C8A6A353496E81F0C0106C82B177.description:
The student demonstrates knowledge and understanding of the Roman Republic and
the Roman Empire.

1030AA2A5CF24CB3BFCEAB335B080BDF.description:
The student tells of the conquests of Alexander of Macedon, the founding of the city of
Alexandria, and the spread of Greek culture in the Hellenistic Period. H

E3E24552B81B42CC98F0B3080CCABF79.description:
The student explains the major ideas of philosophers and religious thinkers in antiquity,
including Siddhartha, Confucius, Thales, Pythagoras, Hippocrates, Socrates, Plato, Aristotle,
and Epicurus, especially in terms of logical reasoning, truth, and ethics. HC

3C955CE50F864A10AA11E1ACBB8F29C6.description:
The student explains the causes, warfare, strategy, outcomes, and effects of the
Peloponnesian War, including the roles of Pericles and Demosthenes. H

826099F8F3804FBD9830F41DCD3CABF9.description:
The student explains the major cultural features and contributions of Athens during the
classical period, including pottery, architecture, sculpture, drama, the Greek language,
institutions, slavery, and the histories of Herodotus and Thucydides. H

AC41C43F2BF543368F5A65389CD4CDFA.description:
The student explains the causes, warfare, strategy, outcomes, and effects of the Persian Wars,
including the battles of Marathon, Thermopylae, and Salamis. H

5BAD509E996B435CA4A6FAFA4D267B20.description:
The student explains why the government of ancient Athens may be considered the beginning
of democracy, including the polis, written constitutions, voting, a legislative body, and the rule
of law. HC

1F3CA5611CBF49D7BB955F3EEFCE9DB4.description: The student identifies the major figures and stories within Greek and Roman mythology. H

0D1269A1EC7145159119173C3E1669E1.description:
The student explains the major historical events, cultural features, and contributions of
civilizations in Peloponnesus and the eastern Mediterranean Sea, including Minoa, Mycenae,
and archaic Sparta and Athens. H

19406E8D1ED241838073269BB3158FDE.description:
The student compares the monotheistic religion of the Hebrews to the traditional polytheism
of the ancient world, including the belief in one god, the Decalogue, individual worth of each
person, and equal moral obligations of each person regardless of class or authority. H

A731BC28F9234AA6A044E4E01622605F.description:
The student explains the major historical events, cultural features, and stories of the ancient
Hebrews, including the origins and role of the Tanakh. H

BDF9BE457B554F91B3DF8BD6278ACEB9.description:
The student explains the major historical events, cultural features, stories, and civil
contributions of Ancient Egypt and Phoenicia, including agriculture, the calendar, hieroglyphic
writing, papyrus, maritime commerce, and the first alphabet. HC

FDDFC5F005AA4F8FB979B3339754A9EF.description:
The student explains the major historical events, cultural features, stories, and civil
contributions of Ancient India, Sumer, Babylon, Assyria, Persia, and Ancient China, including
polytheism, irrigation, metalsmithing, the domestication of animals, slavery, and inventions
such as the wheel, sail, plow, and writing. HC

B390B39BCDEE48CE9EBBCB8E8FF09E0B.description:
The student explains the origins of human beings in Africa and traces the development of
early human civilization through the Neolithic Age, including the roles of climate and
environmental changes, hunter-gatherer societies, metallurgy, and agriculture. H

1AB009666E3A42D69B1BEA190E9B6C52.description:
The student identifies the six characteristics of civilizations: large population centers,
monumental architecture and unique art styles, shared communication strategies, systems for
administering territories, a complex division of labor, and the division of people into social and
economic classes. HCE

E791B1C538194CD5B65D94896EA84C1D.description:
The student demonstrates knowledge and understanding of ancient civilizations in Asia, the
Middle East, northern Africa, and the eastern Mediterranean Sea.

FDB9AC46E222408AA27FA1B38F5BF054.description:
The student can write a persuasive essay of 500-750 words based on class notes, including a
main argument (thesis), topic sentences, supporting evidence from history and class, and clear
attempts to explain how the evidence proves the topic sentences and overall thesis. HCE

090E7865119D4665B5D1C4DF89EEF1F2.description:
The student can write an informative essay of 500-750 words on a historical figure based on
class notes. H

1CC69B3C8E004C858C21B7BA3167F033.description:
The student can write a narrative essay of 500-750 words on a historical event based on class
notes. H

C08C148E1074440799B05CC185971229.description:
Building upon skills learned in previous grades, the student learns the skills to complete the
following tasks, completing each task with relative ease by the end of high school.

F1407A31722940C397CE2D429BCC1119.description:

CG

37DE07400DF84E3DA42983177049D872.description:

and people groups in the world’s places and regions.

FE576A64DDDE4CC2979FDDFE945EF5B9.description:

AC7674B5473946149122235B1E6ACE2D.description:

DEB3EEF6C0434057B4903C64BACF6E03.description:
Major Geographic Features: Indian Ocean, Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, Ganges River,

6CF95E767703433983707B3D2D564763.description:
Major Countries (Cities): Armenia, Azerbaijan, Cyprus, Georgia, Iran (Tehran), Iraq

Qatar, Saudi Arabia (Riyadh, Mecca), Syria (Damascus), Turkey (Istanbul, Ankara),
United Arab Emirates (Dubai), Yemen

1EC12A7FE46B4F2D9A3F8C54CC983715.description:
Major Geographic Features: Black Sea, Mediterranean Sea, Caspian Sea, Red Sea,

349D980589084FBFA88550A141AB1B4C.description:
Major Countries (Cities): Algeria (Algiers), Angola, Botswana, Cameroon, Central

8D4B7EE13EAA40A1A6BA80B07889605C.description:
Major Geographic Features: Mediterranean Sea, Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Sahara
Desert, Nile River, Lake Victoria, Mount Kilimanjaro, Atlas Mountains, the Horn of
Africa, Red Sea, Suez Canal, Cape of Good Hope, Niger River, Congo River, Kalahari
Desert, Congo Rainforest

53FC06A684C34199BA33B0D16F852481.description:
The student can use the six essential elements of geography to describe the following regions
in A thru F subpoints below. The six essential elements of geography are spatial terms, places
and regions, physical systems, human systems, environment and society, and the uses of
geography. G

075BAD257B6948FB8E128BB5DD6B8C4C.description:
The student will construct a map or other geographic representations that demonstrate the
physical and cultural characteristics. G

D9FE1210CA1048DEA32405DB4473E9AA.description:
Students will demonstrate knowledge of applying geospatial resources and tools to interpret and
analyze geographic information.

document.title: South Dakota Social Studies Standards Adopted April 17, 2023

BB08E63487C6462D8CAF244C5CB1FD6B.description:
The student identifies the features and effects of the modern global economy, including the
role of technology, the International Monetary Fund, the Chinese economy, nonprofits, and
nongovernmental organizations. CE

0694FAEBFDC24AA5BC4BE5D0B016EC1E.description:
The student explains the historical (kinship, generosity, trade, and communal stewardship of
land natural resources) and current economies of the Oceti Sakowin (including select
standards from Oceti Sakowin Essential Understandings 1-2 and 5-7), including major
industries, the role of government, and their relationships to the economies of other states
and nations. CE

7D51F1374E59464B9BF89395C254069B.description:
The student explains the historical and current economies of South Dakota and Native
American tribes, including their major industries, the role of government, and their
relationships to the economies of other states and nations. CE

E85C8592C369404DA3F9C3BB2690797B.description:
The student explains the economic ideas of John Maynard Keynes and contrasts them with
those of Ludwig von Mises, Friedrich Hayek, and Milton Friedman. CE

A00BBB0A349A49289267F7039A31D1F4.description:
The student explains the roles of speculation, corruption, war, and government policy in most
major recessions, depressions, and periods of economic growth. CE

39C6A5085C974CA88457ED80D713AA55.description:
The student explains the ways governments have increasingly redistributed more goods and
services in the course of American history. CE

FE91BD3658C64301A97A3351A3937EFA.description:
The student explains that the purpose of government as outlined in the Declaration of
Independence is to “secure these rights.” C

60AD292B5486494EBCF2290FF94801BD.description:
The student explains how general incorporation laws affected the size of businesses and the
effects on competition and workers. CE

D5BB426AD8714CB79472BADEBB4E908D.description:
The student explains the origins and effects of the Agricultural Revolution, the First Industrial
Revolution, and the Enclosure Movement in England, including Adam Smith’s observations on
the capitalist nature of an industrial society. HCE

11EBDE7E33CB40F491D38CF473463F2C.description:
The student explains the history of economic thought and policy prior to the First Industrial
Revolution, including the economies of the ancient and medieval worlds, mercantilism,
slavery, and classical economics. HCE

80EEC85F2E6B4F559BF0CAD9EACFD010.description:
The student demonstrates knowledge and understanding of the historical relationship between
government policy and the economic decisions of individuals and businesses.

F4C21183B0974767B56C912201AF03DD.description:
The student explains the terms and effects of the Smoot-Hawley Tariff, the North American
Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), the
General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), and the World Trade Organization (WTO).
HCE

F079AA8DEBD54F53851BAF0402DC3843.description:
The student explains how exchange rates affect the purchasing power of people in different
countries. E

32932BA7B06049C090EA642588D9DF05.description:
The student explains the purposes, advantages, and disadvantages of trade barriers such as
quotas and tariffs. CE

EC210E7D1BFE41D4A6F6B01724CA2973.description:
The student explains the benefits of trade in true free trade agreements for individuals,
regions, and countries. CE

810A788FC2FE47D8ABCA59B148600CB5.description: The student distinguishes between imports and exports. E

9BECFB86C20A472DADF312C2F56EE06B.description: The student demonstrates knowledge and understanding of trade and commerce.

9662ADB379C348D091185EB630882C30.description:
The student explains how real estate, bullion, stocks, bonds, and mutual funds serve as
investment opportunities. E

D789B9054D3C451292C69915D5F4853F.description:
The student explains the basic savings, investment, and credit services that financial
institutions offer. E

9E159279092E44F1AE263539E90214D6.description:
The student explains the role of banks, including associated advantages, disadvantages, and
risks. E

F21CAEDB82574407A55A20FE5DA13DCB.description:
The student explains how the Federal Reserve can affect the supply and value
(inflation/deflation) of money through buying and selling government bonds, changing bank
reserve ratios, and adjusting the discount interest rate. E

7D2129C15D7F44B193D7533993E8B837.description: The student explains the role of the Federal Reserve within the banking system. E

38273414AB734E738FCB0D8AE4ACE64F.description: The student explains the forms of money in the United States economy. E

F3B5BB16FF6B4BFF954F23BB8CFD428D.description:
The student explains the basic functions of money, including as a medium of exchange, a unit
of account, and a store of value. E

3783C910D44D4BFEA1321D1982284CD7.description: The student demonstrates knowledge and understanding of money and financial institutions.

1D0C228C350543ED92A0E6A55E1DA274.description: The student investigates the maxim of “the unintended consequences of good intentions.” CE

DA91E045D938479DA05668F54F7813F3.description:
The student explains how the costs of government policies and programs do not abide by
economic efficiency once social or political goals influence such policies. CE

788B96642176487E975A02F5F77D10F1.description:
The student explains the ways in which government action may harm the economy, including
excessive taxation, increased money supply, excess government spending, excessive regulation,
political corruption, and nationalization. CE

EBDE79F25EBA438F8B7706781D512B9A.description: The student explains how wage and price controls can create shortages and surpluses. CE

4E9F82F0BBFB48A5A80ACEEF252078D2.description:
The student identifies examples of goods and services that federal, state, local, and tribal
governments manage within the United States and South Dakota. CE

DE1E4FB4C08D4A44902CE01E0495AB8B.description:
The student identifies the traits of natural monopolies and the arguments for and against
government involvement in these fields. CE

D826DA5851CB45B78A41F8C02EDF0C4E.description: The student investigates the maxim that there is “no such thing as a free lunch.” CE

49D1D62F95154A8A8576932CB68A5001.description: The student explains the different uses and functions of fiscal and monetary policy. CE

9CC6274719DC48D7A47D4DE3B8465F11.description:
The student explains taxation and the different kinds of taxation, including income tax, sales
tax, corporate and payroll taxes, Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid, and inflation. CE

DA7BA890ED754076A1FCD6B2A41DA617.description:
The student identifies the major sources of revenue and categories of expenses within
government budgets. CE

70618550B7FA4327A53B6944C3D6621A.description:
The student demonstrates knowledge and understanding of the relationship between government
policy and the economic decisions of individuals and businesses.

D05C97FA0BF546A48892AFF24BA7B2A3.description:
The student explains the different causes of inflation and deflation, including who gains and
loses due to each. E

2B0A13311CD540848B2DE82108223E19.description: The student explains unemployment and economic growth, including how each is calculated. E

6D1437B53168420FBDFF933E56442555.description:
The student explains aggregate supply and demand, Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and Gross
National Production (GNP), including how each is calculated. E

737DFD1B8D974DA9BB1CEA11A351A42F.description: The student explains the phases of the business cycle and its causes. E

9D9A00F2CDEE4A468BE1680BE109AB48.description:
The student demonstrates knowledge and understanding of the business cycle and key economic
macroeconomic measurements.

44619457C904425A87C9EE7208E41A5F.description:
The student explains the differences between perfection competition, oligopoly, monopolistic
competition, and monopoly. E

12DF00E995184EC6878EC4150E574B16.description:
The student explains how wages depend on the market value of the produced good or service
and the productivity of the worker in producing that good or service. E

6EF3D6997CA2450EA9F971F1DAADCE5E.description:
The student explains the virtues and skills required of workers to be successful in the
workplace. E

88F336902B40406E8E5CF6B9135AE811.description:
The student explains the roles of economies of scale, mass production, and the division of
labor, especially in an industrial economy. E

7B8826F84B744F948814C333E2F32550.description:
The student explains how businesses can fund and grow their work through earnings and
profit, stock issues, and borrowing, including the advantages and risks of each. E

70D8D50308DB4B68B2F16212EBF7B611.description:
The student explains the difference between sole proprietorship, partnership, and corporation
within business organization. E

95A4D184574F48BBA4D1F0606B60AC39.description:
The student explains how competition among many sellers reduces the price of goods and
services while encouraging producers to increase production. E

D83BAAF859234E4289AF108C3A4B4AB0.description:
The student demonstrates knowledge and understanding of major market structures within the
United States economy.

480B37237470423EB4ABA7F6C4BC9DF0.description:
The student explains the American founders’ views on private property and its protection, and
the extent to which the average American has been able to own land or a home and securely
hold private property compared to historical and world standards. CE

D745F812CABE431393134CD677BEAB9B.description:
The student explains how defined private property and intellectual property rights and
enforced contracts are necessary in a free market economy. CE

9B84E11F0A334088B499DCDC3E64C6BE.description:
The student explains how the American, and especially the South Dakota, agricultural
economics impact agricultural producers and the agricultural industry as a whole to
understand the trends in domestic and international food systems, commodity prices,
population trends, and trade policies. CE

54D695D5A3884B6AB3FD62FBA0D2280B.description:
The student explains how the American economy has historically been characterized as free
market or capitalist, meaning that the laws allow individuals to possess more goods or
currency than they need to survive; and to invest, produce, distribute, and buy and sell goods
and services by making their own agreements with one another. CE

FAA3D41121ED4842A2B941DE40488320.description:
